lines.en: And when the morning comes, don’t wake. Stay closed, oh tired eyes.
With distance still and bones to break, the shape of our demise-
Shall mold the neon hearts we share, remind us who we are.
Survivors in a dying world. Two strangers in two cars.
Mildew again.
Familiar, but not.
Now masked by the smoke-tendril arms of cheap scented candles, this is nothing like the floor of an old, lived-in apartment.
This is a place where people come to forget under the pretense of making memories. And it is somewhere you never thought you’d see come the morning after.
Tell me, Friend — what did you dream of last night?
Ignore me all you like. It does not change the fact that I grow within you like that dragon grows in her.
: Sensei?...

How comfortable it must be — to have the arms you’ve always dreamt of plunged deep in the stomach of your nightmares — draped over you like the curtains you plucked from the side of the road just last month.
They smell of mildew too, I’m sure. You haven’t learned how to get rid of it yet. And that’s just one of the many things you likely won’t ever learn if you stay where you are now.
: Hah...
Would you like to go back, Yumi?
Because you can.
All you need to do is make a wish.
She lightly removes the arm of the man who comforted her last night, placing it gently by his side as she seizes a very rare opportunity to get a look at his face while he can’t see hers.
Her gaze lingers on his eyes — closed and moving rapidly behind his eyelids like the sockets are full of worker ants. Like his body is their underground lair.
She thinks about removing his glasses. She didn’t want him to risk breaking them if he rolled over now that he wasn’t anchored to her body.
She doesn’t, though.
She just stares at him. Half thankful. Half cherished. Two halves that were entirely unfamiliar to her, yet combined to create something or somewhere that just felt right.
But one good thing in a sea of bad things can not offset that ever-encroaching darkness. And while these halves were good ones, there were two others that always dragged her down.
They followed her everywhere. They determined everything about her life. Yet, she was afraid to leave them behind because she was unsure of what else she might find.
She decides to keep staring..
He decides to wake up.
: What time is it?...
: I don’t know...
: You can go back to sleep, though. It’s fine.
: What are you going to do?...
: I have to get ready for school.
: I imagine it’s still pretty early since I can’t hear anybody fucking anymore.
: School? Are you kidding? Take the day off. You’ve never had a better reason to skip than this.
: Yeah, that’s exactly why I ain’t doin’ it this time.
: Explain?
: The fuck do you think is gonna happen if I just do my own thing again all day?
: Question ain’t for you to answer, numbnuts. It’s one of those rhetorical ones or whatever they’re called.
: If I stay here, I’ll wind up beatin’ myself up until I feel even fuckin’ worse. And you saw me last night. This shit fucking sucks. Figure school will at least distract me.
: I can be a distraction too. Going to school now is-
: You’ve done your part already, okay? I mooch off you any longer and Chika won’t even be able to convince herself she’s “winning” anymore.
: I’ll pay you back for the room as soon as I can. But-
: But...what?
: Uhh...
: Nothing.
: Just...I’ll pay you back as soon as I can. Maybe Noriko can ask the boss to give me an advance on my next paycheck or-
: You don’t need to pay me back. Put it toward getting the power back on at Chika’s old place. I can help you pay the bill.
: I already fuckin’ told you you’ve done enough.
: By spending one night with you and barely saying anything?
: You...hugged me and shit too...
: And that helped?
: Helped me...realize there’s still some shit out there scarier than cancer, yeah.
: Don’t go to school today.
: You ain’t gonna talk me outta this, Sensei...but I...appreciate you looking after me.
: Just want to...try and get shit back to normal. Forget I read anything. Probably just...some kinda misunderstanding anyway.
: Or...we could talk about it.
: We do that too much now.
: Like...don’t you ever miss the days when I was just some fuckin’ delinquent you’d chase around on your quest to fuck every high school girl in Kumon-mi?
: Sometimes. But then I think about things like this and how, if we hadn’t ever become more, that you’d be all alone during the hardest times of your life.
: You mean like what I’m tryin’ to do right now despite you practically beggin’ me to stay?
: Exactly. Now sit back down or I’m going to come back to school for the sole purpose of making sure you have detention every day for the rest of your never-ending school life.
: Never...ending...
: Wait...yeah...
: If we’re fuckin’ stuck here and shit, that means Yuki ain’t gonna go anywhere...right?! Her thing’ll just...reset! Back to normal! Right?!
: Right?...
: I don’t know, Yumi.
: The thing with Makoto’s dad is really the only example we have of death within the timeloops. And it’s not like we can just call him up to see if he’s alive again.
: Like...maybe if we get another call about him dying, we can assume things like that can happen. But without anything to go off of, we’ve just...
: Yeah. Okay. I get it.
: Anyway, school. See you.
: Just like that? You’re not even wearing your uniform.
: My-
: Ahh, fuck. Forgot about that.
: Not exactly...used to spending the night in...seedy love hotels...
: Guess you have no choice but to skip school entirely then.
: It’s barely past five in the morning. I’ve got time to make it to the dorms and get changed beforehand.
: Can I walk you there at least?
: No.
: Why?
: Because walking out of a love hotel with a girl like me ain’t gonna be good for your public image. Nor would be walking me to the dorm while everyone else is getting ready.
: You think I wanna be bombarded by questions right now, man? If I’m alone, people will just do what they always do and avoid me. That’s exactly what I need from everyone but you apparently.
: You’re not even going to tell Chika then? Because I feel like she’d be better at dealing with this sort of thing than literally anyone since she’s essentially gone through it already.
: Yeah, that’s why I said she’s a “whole thing” yesterday.
: Oh. I thought you were just talking more about how my penis broke her.
: Yeah, that definitely doesn’t help. But even if you broke her, she’s still my best friend. I don’t want to bring back bad memories.
: I’m sure she’d be fine with it under the circumstances, Yumi.
: Probably...but still.
: At the very least...talk to your mom. If you can find her, at least.
: She hasn’t exactly been reliable lately, and...I guess now I’m starting to understand why. But I had no idea something like this was-
: Can’t I just ignore it?...
: Can’t we just...try and see if the reset thing takes care of it?
: What if it doesn’t, though?
: Then I guess it’s good I’ve already gotten used to how it feels when she ain’t around.
: Yumi...you don’t mean that.
: Of course I don’t fuckin’ mean that...
: But it’s easier to say than admitting I was starting to fucking forgive her.
: It’s easier to say than thanking her for making an effort for the first time in her fucking life! Easier than letting her try to be a part of mine!
: I was fine without her! She could’ve just stayed gone! But now she’s shown back up, made me realize what I’ve been missing all these years, and she’s just going to leave me again?! What the fuck?!
: Sorry, I...didn’t mean to yell. I know it ain’t your fault.
: You can hit me if you want too. I make a good punching bag in times like this.
: Yeah, I bet you’d fucking like that, wouldn’t you?
: Maybe under happier pretenses, yeah.
: Thank you again. For...all of this.
: Thank you for not reporting me to the police after I assaulted you on a bridge. That single decision is what made it possible for us to grow this close.
: Best thing I’ve ever not done, I guess.
: Have fun at school, Yumi.
: Yeah...I’m off.
Black oak door, carpet floor. Everything you’d want and more!
But just because you’re pining for a place to go to hide from your-
Regrets or past, ole’ childish lore. Not quite recalled, yet not ignored.

All of this shan’t come to pass. Not the chiming of distant bells that signal to you when it’s time to bend, nor the slowly manifesting sound of an EKG that becomes evermore haunting the longer it drones on for.
Could this be a case where you’d want to welcome that pain, though?
Is one’s perpetual suffering worth the joy their presence brings you? And if that person has sinned, would such a fate be deserved?
How much pain is enough for you, Yumi? What is it that you want?
: Bite me.
: Hm? Did you say something?

Yes... acknowledge me! Cultivate me! Let me grow in fields I’ve never seen before! Let me breathe in the stagnant, stale air of love hotels and dilapidated apartments! I can smell the pork broth from here!
: No...just a sigh.
: Oh...Okay then.
: Guess I’ll just...be here.
: Yeah...
: Call me if you need me.
: Yeah...
Go! Experience life! Distract yourself from me! For I will be the one to-
: I said bite me...
: Yumi?
: Did you forget-
: Yes.
: Chu.
: Uhhh...
: Now, I’m off.
: You just kissed me.
: So what? Ain’t like we haven’t done that before. This one had nothing on our first.
: You...just kissed me.
: Yeah...
: You earned it.
: But if you tell anyone, you will die.
: I’m off!
: Yeah...
: Have fun at school...
She thought about something for a second.
She thought about casting aside her typical lone-wolf personality in favor of one who enjoys herself a little more.
But she backtracked the moment she made it onto school grounds and saw the way her peers scattered like roaches once the lights go on.
She turned her phone off shortly after that. It kept ringing, but she didn’t know what to say to the voice she expected to hear on the other end of it.
Soon, her best friend found her. Turns out she had gotten a call as well. So she asked Yumi if everything was alright.
Yumi lied and said yes. It was at that point she began to question everything.
She needed a distraction to distract her from the distraction now.
And so she found one — hyperventilating in the bathroom and telling herself that everything was going to be okay.
It was the youngest she felt in years.
the end.
